message.content:
Let \(a,b\) be independent uniform random variables on \([0,1]\). Rounding to the nearest integer gives

\[
A=\begin{cases}
0 & a<1/2\\
1 & a>1/2
\end{cases}
\qquad
B=\begin{cases}
0 & b<1/2\\
1 & b>1/2
\end{cases}
\]

and since \(c=a+b\),

\[
C=\begin{cases}
0 & c<1/2\\
1 & 1/2<c<3/2\\
2 & c>3/2
\end{cases}
\]

Ties have probability \(0\), so we can ignore them.

We need \(A+B=C\).

- If \(A+B=0\), then \(a<1/2\) and \(b<1/2\), and we need \(C=0\), i.e. \(a+b<1/2\).  
  This region is a triangle with area \(\frac12\cdot \frac12\cdot \frac12=\frac18\).

- If \(A+B=1\), then exactly one of \(a,b\) is greater than \(1/2\).  
  Then \(a+b\) is always between \(1/2\) and \(3/2\), so \(C=1\) automatically.  
  This occurs with probability \(\frac12\).

- If \(A+B=2\), then \(a>1/2\) and \(b>1/2\), and we need \(C=2\), i.e. \(a+b>3/2\).  
  In the square \([1/2,1]^2\), the region \(a+b>3/2\) has area \(\frac18\).

Thus the total probability is

\[
\frac18+\frac12+\frac18=\frac34.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{\frac34}\).
